name: The Consensus Game (Equilibrium-Ranking)
executive_summary: Frame decoding as a signaling game between a generator and discriminator role of the same model, and decode by computing an approximate equilibrium instead of just sampling generatively or scoring discriminatively.
description: Notes that a language model queried generatively (sample an answer) and the same model queried discriminatively (score/rank candidate answers) can give incompatible predictions for the same question — there's no guarantee the two modes agree. This reframes decoding as a regularized imperfect-information signaling game where a 'generator' role tries to communicate a correctness signal via natural language to a 'discriminator' role, and a training-free algorithm (Equilibrium-Ranking) computes an approximate equilibrium of that game to produce the final decoded answer, reconciling the two modes rather than picking one. Reported to let a 7B model outperform much larger 65B/540B models on several benchmarks purely from the decoding procedure.
when_to_use: Tasks where generative and discriminative use of the same model give inconsistent answers, and a training-free decoding-level fix (rather than retraining) is preferred.
when_not_to_use: Simple tasks where generative and discriminative scoring already agree — the equilibrium computation adds cost without a consistency problem to fix.
known_pitfalls: Requires implementing an equilibrium-finding procedure at decode time, which is more involved than standard sampling or reranking and needs a well-defined candidate/scoring setup.

primary_source.title: The Consensus Game: Language Model Generation via Equilibrium Search
